article_title: User Interface Design for E-Learning Software
citation: Behnam Faghih, Mohammad Reza Azadehfar, S. D. Katebi. (2013). User Interface Design for E-Learning Software. The International Journal of Soft Computing and Software Engineering [JSCSE], Vol. 3, No. 3.
title: UIDEL: user interface design for e-learning as the intersection of UI design principles and learning psychology
description: The article proposes that designing the user interface of educational software requires combining conventional UID principles with principles and concepts of learning. It frames UI as "the point of interaction between user and educational body" and argues that educational aims may fail even with good content if this correlation is unsuccessful. The framework organizes its analysis around stimulus/motivation, working memory, multimedia presentation, and availability as UI-relevant learning factors.
requirements: Design must begin with an understanding of the intended users, including profiles of their age, sex, physical abilities, education, cultural or ethnic background, motivation, goals and personality
constraints: The article states it focuses only on psychological issues of user interface design among the many disciplines involved in e-learning
examples: The authors illustrate the framework through educational software they built, showing how UI can improve learning, motivation, and time efficiency
